---
title: "Into the Plane"
---

## Same physics, more geometry

Nothing in the forward model or the filter knows about dimensions. The
potential sums [$-M_j/r_{ij}$](../method/notation-and-glossary.qmd#term-index-conventions) over whatever coordinates you hand it; only
the [prior](../method/notation-and-glossary.qmd#term-prior) gains a column when the mass can hide in a plane instead of on a
line. The interesting changes are *geometric*:

- The eight clocks are scattered **asymmetrically** across the region.
  Reflection of a source around a symmetric layout permutes that layout's
  readings. Because clock channels are labeled, the permuted vector is
  generally distinguishable from the original; a true degeneracy appears
  only if channel identity is discarded or the data vector itself respects
  the permutation. Asymmetry still helps by removing those special cases.
- The clocks sit at a perpendicular offset (`track_offset=3.0`) from the
  mass plane. Without it, a hypothesis that drifts right on top of a clock
  could explain that clock's reading with an arbitrarily small mass — the
  offset keeps the geometry informative.

::: {#demo-2d-text}
Before any reading the dots cover the whole square. The first readings pull
them toward the mass, and by the eighth they are a small cloud around it; the
three traces at the right narrow at the same time. After 50 readings the run
ends at x = 1.42 ± 0.11, y = -1.22 ± 0.11 and M = 0.100 ± 0.001, against a true
x = 1.50, y = -1.00 and M = 0.100. Each ± is one standard deviation of the
final cloud. The y estimate sits about two of those from the truth: that is
this run's noise, and another seed would miss in another direction.
:::

## The surviving hypotheses

Scaled down and executed on this page, here is what the particle cloud looks like after 25
observations:

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
#| renderings: [light, dark]
#| fig-cap:
#|   - "The surviving hypotheses after 25 observations. Dots are particles; the ring and crosshair mark the true mass position."
#|   - "The surviving hypotheses after 25 observations. Dots are particles; the ring and crosshair mark the true mass position."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from clocks import (
    ClockArray, InferenceConfig, MassConfig, NoiseConfig,
    PriorConfig, SimulationConfig, infer, simulate,
)
from clocks.viz import THEMES, show, style

clock_positions = np.array([
    [-4.0, 0.0], [-2.0, 3.0], [1.0, 4.0], [4.0, 2.0],
    [5.0, -1.0], [2.0, -4.0], [-1.0, -3.0], [-3.0, -1.5],
])
clock_array = ClockArray(positions=clock_positions, track_offset=3.0)
truth = MassConfig(positions=np.array([[1.5, -1.0]]), masses=np.array([0.10]))
sim = simulate(SimulationConfig(
    clock_array=clock_array, ground_truth=truth,
    noise=NoiseConfig(observation_std=0.005), n_observations=25, seed=42,
))
result = infer(sim.observations, InferenceConfig(
    clock_array=clock_array, noise=NoiseConfig(observation_std=0.005),
    prior=PriorConfig(position_range=(-8.0, 8.0), mass_range=(0.005, 0.15)),
    n_particles=500, n_masses=1,
    ess_target=0.8, rejuvenation_steps=2, proposal_scale=2.38, seed=42,
))

particles = result.particle_state.particles
true_x, true_y = truth.positions[0]

for theme in THEMES:
    with style(theme) as colors:
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.5, 5.4))
        cloud = ax.scatter(
            particles[:, 0], particles[:, 1],
            s=10, alpha=0.35, linewidths=0, color=colors.belief,
        )
        ring = ax.scatter(
            true_x, true_y, marker="o", s=300,
            facecolors="none", edgecolors=colors.truth, linewidths=1.3,
        )
        crosshair = ax.scatter(
            true_x, true_y, marker="+", s=300,
            color=colors.truth, linewidths=1.3,
        )
        clock_marks = ax.scatter(
            clock_positions[:, 0], clock_positions[:, 1],
            marker="s", s=50, color=colors.ink,
        )
        ax.set_xlabel("x")
        ax.set_ylabel("y")
        ax.set_aspect("equal")
        legend = ax.legend(
            [cloud, (ring, crosshair), clock_marks],
            ["particles", "true position", "clocks"],
        )
        # The cloud's own dots are too small and faint to read as a key.
        legend.legend_handles[0].set_sizes([40])
        legend.legend_handles[0].set_alpha(0.8)
        show(fig)
```

The cloud has collapsed from a uniform smear over a 16×16 box to a small
knot beside the true position, offset from it by about its own width — three
parameters recovered from nothing but tick rates.

::: {.callout-note title="2D costs particles"}
The same posterior precision needs a larger cloud as the parameter count
grows: candidates must cover a volume, not an interval. Three parameters is
still cheap. But this is the curse of dimensionality, and the
[multi-mass pages](two-hidden-masses.qmd) — six parameters — will feel it
properly.
:::
